title: When is the automorphism bound sharp?
content: The parent proved |Aut_F(K)| ≤ [K:F]_s via an injection toEmb of automorphisms into embeddings of K into its algebraic closure, and left two open questions: (1) is the bound an equality for normal K/F? (2) is toEmb then a bijection? This entry answers both at once by recognizing that Mathlib's Normal.algHomEquivAut already packages exactly the needed equivalence, with the parent's toEmb as its inverse. The key emphasis: the equality |Aut_F(K)| = [K:F]_s needs only NORMALITY, not separability — the automorphism group counts the separable degree, reaching the full degree [K:F] exactly in the separable (Galois) case.
mathContext: $|\mathrm{Aut}_F(K)| \le [K:F]_s \le [K:F]$: first $=$ iff normal, second $=$ iff separable, both $=$ iff Galois.

title: The parent's injection is the inverse of Normal.algHomEquivAut
content: The structural insight that makes the whole entry free lives here. toEmb re-declares the parent's post-composition map — an F-automorphism e ↦ (toAlgHom F K (AlgebraicClosure K)).comp e.toAlgHom. Then toEmb_eq_symm_algHomEquivAut shows this hand-built injection is definitionally (proved by rfl) the inverse function of Normal.algHomEquivAut F (AlgebraicClosure K) K: that equivalence's invFun sends σ ↦ (toAlgHom F K _).comp σ.toAlgHom, which is literally toEmb. Recognizing the parent's ad-hoc map as one half of an existing Mathlib equivalence — with no glue lemma needed, just rfl — is what turns two open questions into corollaries.
mathContext: $\mathrm{toEmb} = (\texttt{Normal.algHomEquivAut}\,F\,\overline K\,K)^{-1}$, an equality that holds by $\mathtt{rfl}$.

title: The embedding–automorphism equivalence answers OQ2
content: embEquivAlgEquiv names the equivalence Field.Emb F K ≃ (K ≃ₐ[F] K) for normal K/F — every F-embedding of K into its algebraic closure restricts to an F-automorphism, and conversely. toEmb_bijective then answers open question 2 in one line: since toEmb is the symm of this equivalence, it is bijective via (…).symm.bijective. Normality is exactly the hypothesis that makes this work — it forces every F-embedding into the algebraic closure to land back inside K, so it restricts to an automorphism rather than escaping to a larger field. Without normality only the injection survives, which is precisely the parent's weaker result.

title: The separable-degree equality [K:F]_s = |Aut_F(K)|
content: finSepDegree_eq_card_algEquiv is the headline: for any normal extension K/F, Field.finSepDegree F K = Nat.card (K ≃ₐ[F] K), answering open question 1. Since Field.finSepDegree F K is definitionally Nat.card (Field.Emb F K), this is just Nat.card_congr applied to Normal.algHomEquivAut — no finiteness hypothesis needed (for an infinite normal extension both sides are 0). card_algEquiv_eq_finSepDegree is the symmetric statement, matching the shape of the parent's bound. Mathlib v4.26 records the cardinality equality only under the stronger Galois hypothesis (IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank), so this normal-only equality is genuinely new packaging.

title: Separability boundary and the Galois corollary
content: card_algEquiv_eq_finrank_iff_isSeparable isolates the sharp boundary: among finite normal extensions, |Aut_F(K)| = [K:F] ⟺ K/F is separable (rewrite by the equality, then Field.finSepDegree_eq_finrank_iff). This makes precise that the automorphism group measures the separable degree, not the full degree — for a normal purely inseparable extension [K:F]_s = 1 = |Aut| while [K:F] = pⁿ is arbitrary. card_algEquiv_eq_finrank_of_normal_isSeparable recovers Mathlib's Galois fact IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank (|Aut| = [K:F] for finite Galois) as a one-line corollary — normal equality + finSepDegree_eq_finrank_of_isSeparable — showing the normal equality strictly subsumes the Galois statement.
mathContext: Finite normal $K/F$: $|\mathrm{Aut}_F(K)| = [K:F] \iff K/F$ separable; normal $+$ separable $=$ Galois recovers $|\mathrm{Gal}| = [K:F]$.
